newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish coalition leaders set to meet on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Turkish coalition leaders set to meet on Sunday.

text.p: The leaders of Turkey's crumbling Islamist-led government were set to hold talks on Sunday over ways to solve the deepening crisis around their coalition, a spokesman for Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said.
"I think the meeting will take place this afternoon," the spokesman told Reuters when asked about the timing of a meeting between Ciller and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Newspapers said the two leaders would discuss a government reshuffle and early elections at talks on Sunday.

A minister from Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) said on Saturday elections could be held as early as October to overcome the impasse facing the 11-month-old coalition since the powerful military demanded a crackdown on Islamist activism in February.
"We do not know the certain date but elections could take place in mid-October," state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Health Minister Ismail Karakuyu as saying.
The DYP has been locked in tough bargaining with its Islamist coalition partners over a possible date for early elections in a last-ditch effort to save the coalition.
Erbakan met for four hours on Saturday evening with leading members of his Welfare Party after a monthly meeting of the National Security Council (NSC), state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
At the NSC meeting, the secularist armed forces renewed pressure on Erbakan to curb a rise in Moslem activism since he became prime minister last June.
Ciller has promised her party she would press Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, to let her lead the country to polls as caretaker head of government.

However, the two sides have so far been unable to agree on a date. Turkish press reports say Erbakan was pushing for a quick poll, but Ciller was holding out for a date sometime next spring. Elections would normally be due by the year 2000.
Under the existing coalition protocol, Ciller was to take over the prime minister's office in June of 1998.
